topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Space Warping

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
lecture_lines: Our robot starts at coordinate one, one.
The grid is built on unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
Moving two steps along i-hat shifts its horizontal position.
Adding one step along j-hat reaches the target point.
This movement creates the final vector, three comma two.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate grid (#444444) and a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (0,0) that moves to (2,1) leaving a white vector trace.
Highlight a red vector (#FF0000) for i-hat (1,0) and a green vector (#00FF00) for j-hat (0,1).
Animate a yellow dot (#FFFF00) moving 3 units along i-hat, then 2 units along j-hat to reach (3,2).

sections.title: What is a 'Linear' Transformation?
lecture_lines: A transformation moves every point on our coordinate grid.
Linear transforms rotate and scale the space evenly.
Notice that grid lines always remain parallel and straight.
Squiggly or curved warping is not a linear transformation.
Critically, the origin must never move from the center.
animations: Show a 2D grid (#444444) with several vectors; all vectors smoothly shift to new locations.
Highlight a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (0,0) that remains stationary while the grid around it rotates.
Change grid line colors to cyan (#00FFFF) and scale the grid uniformly to demonstrate spacing.

sections.title: The Secret: Tracking the Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: We only need to track i-hat and j-hat's movements.
Rotating ninety degrees moves them to new landing spots.
These two coordinates fully define how space has warped.
animations: Show the unit vectors i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) on a standard grid, making them thicker for emphasis.
Rotate the basis vectors by 45 degrees; the rest of the grid lines follow them precisely.
Move i-hat to (1,1) and j-hat to (-1,1) while keeping them visible as distinct paths.
Animate a blue vector (#0000FF) at (1,0.5) moving to its corresponding transformed position (0.5, 1.5).
Flash the final transformed grid in light grey (#CCCCCC) while keeping basis vectors highlighted.

sections.title: Matrices: The Coordinate Containers
lecture_lines: A matrix stores these landing spots in its columns.
Stretching the grid updates the matrix with new values.
Columns represent where basis vectors end up after transformation.
animations: Display an empty 2x2 matrix with red brackets (#FF0000) and placeholders.
Move the current coordinates of the transformed i-hat (3,0) into the first column of the matrix.
Move the current coordinates of the transformed j-hat (0,2) into the second column of the matrix.
Show the matrix [[3,0],[0,2]] next to a vector [1,1] and then show the result [3,2].
Apply the transformation [[3,0],[0,2]] to the entire grid, scaling it 3x horizontally and 2x vertically.

sections.title: Application: Transforming 'Yoga Cat'
lecture_lines: Let's apply a shear matrix to our Yoga Cat.
This specific matrix shifts the cat's top horizontally.
Every point on the cat follows the new grid.
A vertex at one, two slides over to three, two.
Matrix math calculates exactly where every point should land.
animations: Create a magenta (#FF00FF) cat-like shape made of connected lines on a grid.
Apply a shear transformation [[1,1],[0,1]] to the cat; the base stays at y=0 while the top shifts right.
Highlight a specific vertex on the cat's ear and show it following a straight horizontal path to its new position.
Briefly show the sheared grid lines in dark blue (#00008B) underneath the cat.
Display the calculation '(1,2) becomes (3,2)' in white text (#FFFFFF) next to the cat's ear vertex.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Every matrix represents a geometric dance of coordinate space.
Matrices are simple maps for complex spatial transformations.
These numbers describe how we warp and shape reality.
animations: Fade in a 2x2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] in gold (#FFD700) and overlay it on a dynamic grid.
Animate the grid quickly cycling through a rotation, then a scale, then a shear.
Fade out all elements except the matrix and the text 'Geometric Maps' in bright green (#00FF00).
